lines: Variant Perception CIO Tian Yang argues governments face an 'impossible trinity' of sovereignty, social spending and sound money, and history suggests sound money is sacrificed first when nations mobilize for military and technological rivalry.
Yang frames AI, with Nvidia at its center, as a national security imperative rather than a purely commercial bet, which puts a floor under investment regardless of near-term returns.

The AI race is described as a 'Sisyphean marathon' of endless, costly financing sprints for compute, creating a persistent inflationary impulse, with a parallel drawn to the 1960s when guns-and-butter spending eroded monetary discipline.

Yang expects the push for chip independence and re-industrialization to replace just-in-time globalization with hard borders, physical rationing and possibly capital controls, and governments to lean on financial repression such as forcing banks to hold government debt.
For investors, Yang warns that sovereignty creates binary event risks such as export bans, capital controls and asset freezes that can outweigh traditional valuation work.
title: The Impossible Trilemma That Hangs Over the Nvidia Crisis
